text: Fission [Lat. fissus , a cleft]: Ger. Theilung ; Fr. scissiparité ; Ital. scissiparità . A method of asexual reproduction among unicellular organisms, the lower Metozoa and the unicellular elements of Metozoa, in which the parent divides into two, often unequal parts. Each half subsequently grows into a complete organism similar to the parent. This process of reproduction is called schizogamy. In the elements of Metozoa the resulting daughter-cells rarely entirely separate. Cf. AGAMOGENESIS and CELL DIVISION. ( C.LL.M. - E.S.G. )
